To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. We propose a novel co-attention model for VQA.

(1) we introduce a novel co attention mechanism that jointly reasons about the question and the image to compute an attention mask for each, and why it is important for answering VQA questions, and (2) we introduce a hierarchical attention model that computes the question attention and image attention in a two stage manner, why it is important, and (3) we present a new dataset called COCO QA that is a combination of the Visual Genome dataset and the COCO captions dataset.

1) co attention is a simple and effective way to improve the performance of VQA and COCO QA, 2) a hierarchical attention mechanism is able to model the complex interaction between question words and image content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of visual question answering.

the following questions: (i) What is the right way to model image region importance and question importance? (ii) How to use the image and question attention for answering a question? (iii) What is the best way to learn these two attentions?
the question of whether the VQA model can be improved by combining visual cues and question attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our paper is a solid contribution that is well presented and well written and is a significant contribution to the VQA literature, but it is not a new state of the art result.
the proposed model has a good performance on the VQA and the COCO QA datasets.

our proposed model is a novel attention model that is capable of modeling "where to attend" and "what to listen" in the image and question simultaneously, and thus, is a highly promising approach to VQA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new, highly specific head- to- head comparison between two strong networks on two strong datasets where our attention- based approach outperforms the baseline.

we show that the co attention model can integrate the temporal hierarchy to attend to the important words in the question while maintaining the spatial hierarchy to attend to image regions, thus improving on existing state of the art for this task.
in addition to the visual module, an attention driven question-aware module is important for improving the performance on VQA tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show how to integrate relevant context into VQA.
it emphasizes the overall importance of a multiscale Pyramidal Hierarchical Attention Architecture for VQA.
we show the importance of integrating question understanding in VQA instead of treating it as 'another feature'.
